html:
Knucati is the map's name for a people of the Tennessee River valley in northern Alabama in the 1500s. The name is not found in the usual sources, and who they were is not clear.

In the 1500s this valley was home to Muskogean-speaking farming towns, late heirs of the Mississippian world. The paramount chiefdom of Coosa lay just to the east, and Hernando de Soto crossed the region in 1540. The Koasati lived on this stretch of the Tennessee River at the time, so they may be the people meant. Like their neighbours, they later moved south and joined the Creek confederacy.
